Sources also consulted (no new verified entries): AD 2.22 LLBG (https://e-aip.azurefd.net/2025-10-02-AIRAC/html/eAIP/LL-AD-2.LLBG-en-GB.html — references Domestic AIP A-07/B-03 for CVFR routes, not in eAIP), AD 2.22 LLER (https://e-aip.azurefd.net/2025-10-02-AIRAC/html/eAIP/LL-AD-2.LLER-en-GB.html — no named CVFR transfer points), GEN 3.4 (https://e-aip.azurefd.net/2025-10-02-AIRAC/html/eAIP/LL-GEN-3.4-en-GB.html), ENR 6-1 ATS Routes chart (https://www.scribd.com/document/936210641/LL-ENR-6-1-en), Wikimedia Commons IsraelCVFRchart-center.jpg (2009 reference), GitHub code search 'commChange' / 'TYONA' / 'Israel CVFR' (no relevant hits). LLHZ, LLIB, LLOV AD 2 pages return HTTP 404 in the public eAIP (domestic-only airfields). Last verified 2026-05-28.
_definition: Each entry marks a CVFR reporting point where pilots are expected to switch ATC frequencies because the point sits on (or at) a sector / CTR / TMA boundary. The chart annotation may be on the boundary line itself rather than directly at the point — the dataset records the *point of change*, not the chart-text position.
_NOTE: TYONA was initially retracted in d4ef4a1 because the chart annotation 'פלוטו מע.' labels the Pluto/Palmachim sector-boundary line rather than the TYONA dot itself. Restored after clarification: TYONA is the reporting point at which pilots cross that boundary, so it IS a comm-change point under the dataset's point-of-change semantics (see _definition). Lesson: chart-text position does not always coincide with the point being annotated; record the point where pilots act. Entries with verified=false are POSITIONAL INFERENCES from the published PLUTO/HAGAV sector-boundary line in ENR 2.1 — they identify reporting points that *geometrically* sit on or near the boundary, but the actual chart 'מעבר תקשורת' symbol placement requires visual inspection of the paper IAA CVFR chart (or PAMAT chapter B-03), which is graphical and not extractable from the published PDF text.

LLHZ (Herzliya) CTR boundary points — LLHZ AD 2 page is 404 in public eAIP, so the per-point handoff list requires PAMAT chapter B-03 / chart access.
LLIB (Rosh Pina) CTR / Galilee corridor — same; LLIB AD 2 page is 404 in public eAIP.
LLOV (Ovda) corridor — same; LLOV AD 2 page is 404 in public eAIP.

Negev / Eilat corridor reporting points (BMNUH, ZOFAR, RUHOT, OVDAT, HAZVA, HRGVS area; SOUTH CONTROL ↔ Eilat APP/TWR transitions) — LLER AD 2.22 does not name any CVFR transfer points (only NURIT for IFR). Requires PAMAT/chart access.

Tel-Aviv → Haifa coastal route mid-segment handoffs (BAZRA, HADRA, FRDIS, BOREN entries below) flagged as candidate handoff points based on geometry + user-supplied hypothesis; require chart confirmation. Frequencies omitted because the actual sector handling depends on altitude (LLBG TMA inside vs. outside) and route lateral position (overwater Tel-Aviv Control vs. overland PLUTO West).
